thread.title: Baylor softball falls to UT Arlington in close 5-4 midweek game
thread.title_full: Baylor softball falls to UT Arlington in close 5-4 midweek game

author: k. b. ramos
title: Baylor softball falls to UT Arlington in close 5-4 midweek game
text:
Baylor softball lost a close game to UT Arlington, 5-4, on Wednesday afternoon at Allan Saxe Field. The Bears built an early three-run lead through the first two innings, but the Mavericks came back with a four-run fourth inning and held on for the win.
The matchup was significant as Baylor looked to maintain momentum before returning to Big 12 conference play. Despite taking an early advantage, mistakes allowed UT Arlington to take control of the game in the middle innings.
Baylor started strong by scoring two runs in the first inning. Brooklyn Carter reached base on an error and later scored on Amber Toven’s RBI single. Another run crossed home plate after a passed ball gave Baylor a 2-0 lead. UT Arlington responded quickly with a sacrifice fly in their half of the first inning.
In the second inning, Carter scored again from first base following another Maverick error, and Toven added a sacrifice fly that extended Baylor’s lead to 4-1. However, UT Arlington capitalized on several Baylor errors during their four-run fourth inning that put them ahead for good at 5-4. The Bears had opportunities late in the game but were unable to score against UTA reliever Maddie Furniss.
Several individual performances stood out for Baylor: one player extended her career-best on-base streak to 20 games; another drove in two runs for her ninth multi-RBI game this season; one led with two hits marking her ninth multi-hit outing this year; another now has a team-high eleven doubles; and yet another leads in hit by pitches. One pitcher scattered three hits over three innings while allowing just one run and three walks.
Looking ahead, Baylor will resume Big 12 play with a series against No. 23 Kansas Jayhawks starting Friday evening in Lawrence, Kansas. All remaining games this season will be televised on ESPN+ and broadcast via radio.
